page.name: Payment reminders
page.h1: Send the reminder before the payment fails
page.metaTitle: Payment reminders on a schedule you control
page.metaDescription: Payment-due reminders sent on a schedule you control, kept transactional, and paced so a due-date batch drains predictably.
page.lede: The reminder that arrives before a due date is a service; the one that arrives after is a complaint notification. Send both, keep them transactional, and pace the due-date batch so it drains in a time you can plan around.

bullets: Before the due date — the reminder that prevents a failure
On a failed payment — the notice that says the payment did not go through
After a grace period — the last notice before the consequence is applied
p: The first one does most of the work. A reminder that arrives before the date is a service; one that arrives after is a complaint notification.

sections.h: Due dates cluster — pace the batch
p: Customers choose the same few billing dates, which turns reminders into a batch. The platform paces a batch to what the provider allows per sender number, so a due-date run stretches predictably instead of failing partway through.
bullets: Per-number pacing so a billing-date batch drains in a known time
Delivery receipts recorded per send, where the provider reports them
Failures retained with the provider’s reason

sections.h: Send a link to the bill, not the bill
p: Amounts and account details are exactly the kind of content that should be resolved behind a login rather than carried in a message. Send a link to the bill, not the bill.

faq.a: It is transactional when the recipient owes the message — a due date or a failed payment. It becomes promotional when it carries an offer, and the consent rules follow the content.

faq.q: Can reminders be scheduled ahead of time?
faq.a: Scheduled and bulk sending exist as console features; their behavior is documented in the help center.

faq.q: What happens to reminders if a provider stops working?
faq.a: On the SMS channel, traffic can route to another connected account rather than failing outright.
